projects.name: 3.1.1.1 Provide technical and financial support to government and non government actors to expand and sustainably provide  high impact food security and nutrition interventions for vulnerable and marginalised population especially adolescents and women of reproductive age in development and humanitarian situations
projects.description:
UNHCR
UNHCR
Achievements: The food security sector continues to contribute to Strategic Development Goal 2.1 by improving access to nutritious food among refugees and asylum seekers in the 13 refugee settlements in Uganda. Furthermore, the sector promotes the self-reliance of refugee communities through complimentary activities. The partners reached 1.39 million beneficiaries through the provision of in-kind food as well as cash-based transfers by the end of Q2. However, owing to the prioritization exercise conducted in July 2023, there was a reduction of 14% of beneficiaries who received in-kind assistance and 6% reduction in cash assistance. Additionally, the further reduction in in-kind rations in most refugee settlements due to limitations in funding increased cash enrolments since beneficiaries preferred cash to the reduced rations. Overall, the proportion of beneficiaries who received cash assistance increased from 60% to 63% from Q1 to Q4. 
Digital cash transfer mechanisms through agent banking continued to be scaled up, and cash beneficiaries owning bank accounts increased from 36 percent to 41 percent out of the overall total cash beneficiaries by the end of the year. To increase access to digital payment instruments, Mobile money will start in Kyangwali and Kiryandogo settlements. In addition to increasing access to digital payment instruments through agency banking, cash beneficiaries received financial literacy skills. A total of 2,954 beneficiaries were trained during the reporting period across all 13 settlements. Efforts to mitigate malnutrition continue to be strengthened through building the capacity of health workers, Village Health Teams (VHTs), and other community structures in providing Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) knowledge to promote better household nutrition. Similarly, active case findings have supported in managing the nutrition situation in the settlements. Currently, the recovery rate remains above the threshold with an average of 93% discharged as cured from the programme within the reporting period.

projects.description:
UNHCR
Achievements: In the Health Sector, the Under-5 mortality remained below the standard of <1.5/1,000. Mosquito net distribution, Indoor residual spraying (iRS) as well as Integrated community case management (iCCM) have ensured that mortalities are contained. Measles vaccination coverage was (83%) against the standard of 95% mainly due to vaccine stockouts as well as the increased number of new refugees. The consultations per clinician per day were higher for the Congolese (DRC) population (65) than for the South Sudan (SSD) population (40) than the acceptable standard of 50 consultations per clinician per day. During the reporting period, the health partners have identified and treated 7,874 children and 2,662 pregnant and lactating women for acute malnutrition, with a cure rate of 71.5%. There are however still challenges with the identification of all HIV positives and initiation on treatment standing at 81.8% and 89.5% though the viral load suppression is better at 92.5% against UNAIDs targets of 95:95:95. With the commitment of the Ministry of Health, support of development partners, 85 out of 101 facilities have been coded. There are more temporary facilities in locations hosting South Sudanese refugees which would not fit the criteria for transition. Efforts are ongoing to develop district transition plans and national transition guidelines to guide and fast track transition of health facilities to the MOH and district local government. All locations were able to continue to hold settlement-level coordination meetings with the co-leadership of the district and the involvement of the different partners.

projects.description:
UNHCR
UNHCR
Achievements: The food security sector continues to contribute to Strategic Development Goal 2.1 by improving access to nutritious food among refugees and asylum seekers in the 13 refugee settlements in Uganda. Furthermore, the sector promotes the self-reliance of refugee communities through complimentary activities. The partners reached 1.39 million beneficiaries through the provision of in-kind food as well as cash-based transfers by the end of Q2. However, owing to the prioritization exercise conducted in July 2023, there was a reduction of 14% of beneficiaries who received in-kind assistance and 6% reduction in cash assistance. Additionally, the further reduction in in-kind rations in most refugee settlements due to limitations in funding increased cash enrolments since beneficiaries preferred cash to the reduced rations. Overall, the proportion of beneficiaries who received cash assistance increased from 60% to 63% from Q1 to Q4. 
Digital cash transfer mechanisms through agent banking continued to be scaled up, and cash beneficiaries owning bank accounts increased from 36 percent to 41 percent out of the overall total cash beneficiaries by the end of the year. To increase access to digital payment instruments, Mobile money will start in Kyangwali and Kiryandogo settlements. In addition to increasing access to digital payment instruments through agency banking, cash beneficiaries received financial literacy skills. A total of 2,954 beneficiaries were trained during the reporting period across all 13 settlements. Efforts to mitigate malnutrition continue to be strengthened through building the capacity of health workers, Village Health Teams (VHTs), and other community structures in providing Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) knowledge to promote better household nutrition. Similarly, active case findings have supported in managing the nutrition situation in the settlements. Currently, the recovery rate remains above the threshold with an average of 93% discharged as cured from the programme within the reporting period.

projects.description:

Mosquito net distribution, Indoor residual spraying (iRS) as well as Integrated community case management (iCCM) have ensured that mortalities are contained. There are however still challenges with the identification of all HIV positives and initiation on treatment standing at 81.8% and 89.5% though the viral load suppression is better at 92.5% against UNAIDs targets of 95:95:95. With the commitment of the Ministry of Health, support of development partners, 85 out of 101 facilities have been coded. There are more temporary facilities in locations hosting South Sudanese refugees which would not fit the criteria for transition. projects.description:
UNHCR
Achievements: In the Health Sector, the Under-5 mortality remained below the standard of <1.5/1,000. Mosquito net distribution, Indoor residual spraying (iRS) as well as Integrated community case management (iCCM) have ensured that mortalities are contained. Measles vaccination coverage was (83%) against the standard of 95% mainly due to vaccine stockouts as well as the increased number of new refugees. The consultations per clinician per day were higher for the Congolese (DRC) population (65) than for the South Sudan (SSD) population (40) than the acceptable standard of 50 consultations per clinician per day. During the reporting period, the health partners have identified and treated 7,874 children and 2,662 pregnant and lactating women for acute malnutrition, with a cure rate of 71.5%. The Refugee Population-based HIV Impact Assessment (RUPHIA) revealed the gains in HIV epidemic control with the prevalence reported at 1.5% (1.8% females and 1.1% Males) 15 years and above. There are however still challenges with the identification of all HIV positives and initiation on treatment standing at 81.8% and 89.5% though the viral load suppression is better at 92.5% against UNAIDs targets of 95:95:95. With the commitment of the Ministry of Health, support of development partners, 85 out of 101 facilities have been coded. There are more temporary facilities in locations hosting South Sudanese refugees which would not fit the criteria for transition. Efforts are ongoing to develop district transition plans and national transition guidelines to guide and fast track transition of health facilities to the MOH and district local government. All locations were able to continue to hold settlement-level coordination meetings with the co-leadership of the district and the involvement of the different partners.

projects.name: 3.1.1.1 Provide technical and financial support to government and non government actors to expand and sustainably provide  high impact food security and nutrition interventions for vulnerable and marginalised population especially adolescents and women of reproductive age in development and humanitarian situations
projects.description:
UNHCR
UNHCR
Achievements: The food security sector continues to contribute to Strategic Development Goal 2.1 by improving access to nutritious food among refugees and asylum seekers in the 13 refugee settlements in Uganda. Furthermore, the sector promotes the self-reliance of refugee communities through complimentary activities. The partners reached 1.39 million beneficiaries through the provision of in-kind food as well as cash-based transfers by the end of Q2. However, owing to the prioritization exercise conducted in July 2023, there was a reduction of 14% of beneficiaries who received in-kind assistance and 6% reduction in cash assistance. Additionally, the further reduction in in-kind rations in most refugee settlements due to limitations in funding increased cash enrolments since beneficiaries preferred cash to the reduced rations. Overall, the proportion of beneficiaries who received cash assistance increased from 60% to 63% from Q1 to Q4. 
Digital cash transfer mechanisms through agent banking continued to be scaled up, and cash beneficiaries owning bank accounts increased from 36 percent to 41 percent out of the overall total cash beneficiaries by the end of the year. To increase access to digital payment instruments, Mobile money will start in Kyangwali and Kiryandogo settlements. In addition to increasing access to digital payment instruments through agency banking, cash beneficiaries received financial literacy skills. A total of 2,954 beneficiaries were trained during the reporting period across all 13 settlements. Efforts to mitigate malnutrition continue to be strengthened through building the capacity of health workers, Village Health Teams (VHTs), and other community structures in providing Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) knowledge to promote better household nutrition. Similarly, active case findings have supported in managing the nutrition situation in the settlements. Currently, the recovery rate remains above the threshold with an average of 93% discharged as cured from the programme within the reporting period.

projects.name: 3.1.1.1 Provide technical and financial support to government and non government actors to expand and sustainably provide  high impact food security and nutrition interventions for vulnerable and marginalised population especially adolescents and women of reproductive age in development and humanitarian situations
projects.description:
UNHCR
UNHCR
Achievements: The food security sector continues to contribute to Strategic Development Goal 2.1 by improving access to nutritious food among refugees and asylum seekers in the 13 refugee settlements in Uganda. Furthermore, the sector promotes the self-reliance of refugee communities through complimentary activities. The partners reached 1.39 million beneficiaries through the provision of in-kind food as well as cash-based transfers by the end of Q2. However, owing to the prioritization exercise conducted in July 2023, there was a reduction of 14% of beneficiaries who received in-kind assistance and 6% reduction in cash assistance. Additionally, the further reduction in in-kind rations in most refugee settlements due to limitations in funding increased cash enrolments since beneficiaries preferred cash to the reduced rations. Overall, the proportion of beneficiaries who received cash assistance increased from 60% to 63% from Q1 to Q4. 
Digital cash transfer mechanisms through agent banking continued to be scaled up, and cash beneficiaries owning bank accounts increased from 36 percent to 41 percent out of the overall total cash beneficiaries by the end of the year. To increase access to digital payment instruments, Mobile money will start in Kyangwali and Kiryandogo settlements. In addition to increasing access to digital payment instruments through agency banking, cash beneficiaries received financial literacy skills. A total of 2,954 beneficiaries were trained during the reporting period across all 13 settlements. Efforts to mitigate malnutrition continue to be strengthened through building the capacity of health workers, Village Health Teams (VHTs), and other community structures in providing Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) knowledge to promote better household nutrition. Similarly, active case findings have supported in managing the nutrition situation in the settlements. Currently, the recovery rate remains above the threshold with an average of 93% discharged as cured from the programme within the reporting period.

projects.name: 3.1.1.6 Provide technical and financial assistance to government and non-government actors to increase access  to gender inclusive and equitable health services including SRH, Mental Health, NCD prevention and control for all especially vulnerable and marginalised.
projects.description:
UNHCR
Achievements: In the Health Sector, the Under-5 mortality remained below the standard of <1.5/1,000. Mosquito net distribution, Indoor residual spraying (iRS) as well as Integrated community case management (iCCM) have ensured that mortalities are contained. Measles vaccination coverage was (83%) against the standard of 95% mainly due to vaccine stockouts as well as the increased number of new refugees. The consultations per clinician per day were higher for the Congolese (DRC) population (65) than for the South Sudan (SSD) population (40) than the acceptable standard of 50 consultations per clinician per day. During the reporting period, the health partners have identified and treated 7,874 children and 2,662 pregnant and lactating women for acute malnutrition, with a cure rate of 71.5%. The Refugee Population-based HIV Impact Assessment (RUPHIA) revealed the gains in HIV epidemic control with the prevalence reported at 1.5% (1.8% females and 1.1% Males) 15 years and above. There are however still challenges with the identification of all HIV positives and initiation on treatment standing at 81.8% and 89.5% though the viral load suppression is better at 92.5% against UNAIDs targets of 95:95:95. With the commitment of the Ministry of Health, support of development partners, 85 out of 101 facilities have been coded. There are more temporary facilities in locations hosting South Sudanese refugees which would not fit the criteria for transition. Efforts are ongoing to develop district transition plans and national transition guidelines to guide and fast track transition of health facilities to the MOH and district local government. All locations were able to continue to hold settlement-level coordination meetings with the co-leadership of the district and the involvement of the different partners.

projects.name: 3.1.1.6 Provide technical and financial assistance to government and non-government actors to increase access  to gender inclusive and equitable health services including SRH, Mental Health, NCD prevention and control for all especially vulnerable and marginalised.
projects.description:
UNHCR
Achievements: In the Health Sector, the Under-5 mortality remained below the standard of <1.5/1,000. Mosquito net distribution, Indoor residual spraying (iRS) as well as Integrated community case management (iCCM) have ensured that mortalities are contained. Measles vaccination coverage was (83%) against the standard of 95% mainly due to vaccine stockouts as well as the increased number of new refugees. The consultations per clinician per day were higher for the Congolese (DRC) population (65) than for the South Sudan (SSD) population (40) than the acceptable standard of 50 consultations per clinician per day. During the reporting period, the health partners have identified and treated 7,874 children and 2,662 pregnant and lactating women for acute malnutrition, with a cure rate of 71.5%. The Refugee Population-based HIV Impact Assessment (RUPHIA) revealed the gains in HIV epidemic control with the prevalence reported at 1.5% (1.8% females and 1.1% Males) 15 years and above. There are however still challenges with the identification of all HIV positives and initiation on treatment standing at 81.8% and 89.5% though the viral load suppression is better at 92.5% against UNAIDs targets of 95:95:95. With the commitment of the Ministry of Health, support of development partners, 85 out of 101 facilities have been coded. There are more temporary facilities in locations hosting South Sudanese refugees which would not fit the criteria for transition. Efforts are ongoing to develop district transition plans and national transition guidelines to guide and fast track transition of health facilities to the MOH and district local government. All locations were able to continue to hold settlement-level coordination meetings with the co-leadership of the district and the involvement of the different partners.

framework.name: STRATEGIC PRIORITY 3: HUMAN WELLBEING AND RESILIENCE
framework.description: WFP’s work under SP3 aims at enhancing the capacities of Government institutions to coordinate and manage food security and nutrition programmes, respond to shocks, address risks and vulnerabilities, enhance livelihoods and resilience of vulnerable populations across the life cycle as a contribution to SDG target 17.9. The Strategic Outcome is organised into two activities. The first is Activity 8. This is responsible for strengthening institutions and systems to deliver social protection programmes and is delivered through the Child Sensitive Social Protection Programme (CSSP). The second is activity 9 and this is charged with building the capacity of institutions to respond to shocks through the Strengthening Shock Responsive Systems in Karamoja (PRO-ACT) project.
